name: Zhongshan Road Old Town (Siming)
tagline: Arcaded streets and the ferry to Gulangyu
description: The historic core of Siming District, where colonnaded qilou shopfronts run down to the harbour and the Gulangyu ferry pier. Snack streets, old teahouses and boutique guesthouses fill the lanes behind. Dense, flat and fully walkable, with metro Line 1 running underneath.
bestFor: Nomads who want to live without a scooter and be surrounded by old Xiamen.
pros: Ferries, seafront promenade and street food at the door
cons: Heavy tourist foot traffic on the main pedestrian streets
Old buildings with poor sound insulation and no lift
Tourist pricing on food along Zhongshan Road itself

name: Zengcuo'an
tagline: Converted fishing village turned cafe hub
description: A former fishing village on the south coast, now a warren of narrow lanes packed with independent cafes, guesthouses, live music bars and craft stalls, right behind the Huandao Road beach. Students from nearby Xiamen University and young Chinese creatives dominate. The closest thing Xiamen has to a nomad quarter.
bestFor: Cafe-hoppers and creatives who want beach access and cheap monthly guesthouse rooms.
pros: Enormous cafe density, easy to work from
Beach and the coastal cycling path minutes away
Cheap monthly rates in converted village houses
cons: Packed with domestic tourists at weekends and holidays
Lanes are cramped, damp and noisy at night
Long metro or bus ride to the business districts

name: Software Park Phase II
description: A landscaped campus of low-rise tech offices between the hills and the sea, housing much of Xiamen's software and gaming industry. Canteens, coffee chains, gyms and new residential blocks serve the engineers who work here. Practical rather than pretty, with fast internet and reliable infrastructure.
bestFor: Developers and startup people who want to be near Xiamen's actual tech scene.
pros: Best connectivity and newest office stock in the city
Modern apartments with lifts and proper gyms
Coastal road and beaches a short ride south
cons: Dead in the evenings and at weekends
Corporate atmosphere with little local character
Rents pushed up by tech salaries

name: Wuyuanwan (Huli)
description: A planned waterfront district around Five Yuan Bay in Huli, built with a wetland park, a yacht marina, wide cycling paths and high-end residential towers. It draws families and better-paid professionals who want space and clean air. Metro Line 3 links it back to the island centre.
bestFor: Nomads with a bigger budget who want a modern flat, a park and sea air.
pros: New towers with pools, gyms and management
Wetland park, marina and safe cycle routes
cons: Sparse nightlife and few independent cafes
Feels sterile compared to old Siming

name: Jimei
description: A mainland district north of the island built around Jimei University and the Tan Kah Kee school complex, with its distinctive swallowtail-roofed architecture, a long waterfront promenade and a big student population. Rents run far below Siming and street food is cheap. Metro Line 1 crosses the sea to get here.
bestFor: Budget nomads and long-stayers who will trade a commute for half the rent.
pros: Rents roughly half of central Siming
Very cheap student food and services
Handsome campus architecture and a seafront walk
cons: Around 40 minutes by metro to the island centre
Almost no English spoken or foreign community
